original: 2 progress, grapple reduction, or squares of push.
revised: 2 progress, grapple reduction, or 2 squares of push.
reason: Missing push numeral; intended distance is 2 squares.

original: 3 progress, grapple reduction, or squares of push.
revised: 3 progress, grapple reduction, or 3 squares of push.
reason: Missing push numeral; intended distance is 3 squares.

original: Proposal: the ally gains 1 Boon to that task’s next roll before the start of your next turn.
revised: The ally gains 1 Boon to that task’s next roll before the start of your next turn.
reason: Removes draft-stage proposal language from an approved card.

original: Stabilize at 0 HP and clear death marks.
revised: Stabilize a Dying character at 0 HP and clear death marks.
reason: Adds the missing target/object to the sentence.

original: One of your summons within its tether.
revised: One of your summons within 6 squares of you (its tether).
reason: “Its tether” is ambiguous; summoning rules use 6 squares.

original: None — no separate roll; resolve Basic Melee using Brawn
reason: Keeps the Attribute column to an attribute; the procedure remains in Rules.

original: Stubborn as Bedrock
reason: Bruce approved keeping the simple +1 HP trait and renaming it to better match the mechanic.

original: The Mountain Remembers
reason: The trait is broader stone expertise; Stone Mason matches the mechanic better.

original: Gain 1 Boon to examining stonework for an unsafe passage, concealed join or later alteration. Obvious construction clues need no roll; the trait does not reveal an untouched wall’s far side.
revised: Gain 1 Boon to rolls to examine or craft with stone. This covers judging craftsmanship, recognizing stone type and origin, reading patina or recent toolwork, finding secret passages or traps built into stone, and spotting weaknesses in stone or stone structures. Obvious construction clues need no roll; this trait does not reveal an untouched wall’s far side.
reason: Bruce expanded the trait to general stone inspection and crafting, including traps, passages, stone type/patina and structural weakness.
notes: Stable ID unchanged; no through-wall detection.

original: While standing on solid ground, gain 1 Boon to defense against forced movement. This is not immunity and does not reduce the resulting distance separately.
revised: Stability +1. You gain 1 Boon to Guile rolls.
reason: Bruce replaced the situational forced-movement Boon with Stability +1 and a blanket Guile Boon; the strong social offset is deliberate.
notes: Stability uses the normal max 3 / highest source and does not protect against Prone. Blanket Guile Boon intentionally offsets Stability 1.

original: Your thumb finds the seam; your ear knows the ring of sound metal.
revised: Your hands know the difference between a quick fix and honest work — and you refuse to settle for the former.
reason: The old narrative described inspection; the trait is now about crafting and craftsmanship.

original: After handling an ordinary metal or stone item, recognize shoddy workmanship and common material without a roll. Gain 1 Boon when a consequential inspection seeks subtler defects. This is not crafting or magical identification permission.
revised: Once per day, after you make a roll to craft or repair an item, you may improve the result by one step: Weak becomes Standard, or Standard becomes Strong. A Strong result is unchanged.
reason: Bruce rejected the inspection focus; the trait should be about crafting and craftsmanship, with a once-per-day result bump.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. Stone Mason owns stone; this trait owns general crafting.

original: Once per combat, after a creature damages you, gain 1 Boon to your next attack against it before the end of your next turn. Choose whether to invoke the trait when the damage occurs. No damage bonus or extra attack.
revised: The first creature that deals damage to you in each combat becomes the mark of your grudge. You gain 1 Boon to attack rolls against each creature marked by your grudge. A creature remains marked forever, even if it escapes; a creature can be marked only once, and additional damage does not add more Boons. You can hold any number of grudges. This grants no damage bonus or extra attack.
reason: Bruce replaced the once-per-combat retaliation with persistent grudges: one new mark per combat, no cap, and no stacking on a creature already marked.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. A dwarf can hold many grudges.

original: Natural undergrowth does not increase the cost of your voluntary movement. Other difficult terrain, forced movement and occupied-square rules are unchanged.
revised: In woodlands and forests, you ignore difficult terrain. This includes difficult terrain caused by natural terrain or obstacles, such as roots, undergrowth, fallen leaves and uneven natural ground. Solid obstacles, occupied squares and magically created or manipulated difficult terrain still apply. Your Speed increases by 1 while you are in woodlands, forests or similar wooded terrain.
reason: Bruce broadened the trait to natural woodland difficult terrain and added +1 Speed while in wooded terrain; final wording explicitly uses the rules phrase ‘ignore difficult terrain’.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. Strong in woodland, inert outside it.

original: Choose one place or community you knew in an earlier age. Gain 1 Boon to Knowledge or Reason rolls recalling its history, people or construction. The DA can tell you what you genuinely witnessed without a roll; memory reveals no events you never knew.
revised: Once per day, before you make a Knowledge or Reason roll, you may call on the knowledge of your ancestors to gain 1 Boon to that roll.
reason: Bruce reframed the trait around the Elves’ interconnected ancestral minds: once per day, 1 Boon to Knowledge or Reason.

original: You pause beside the broken road and recall the voices of the people who laid its first stones.
revised: You pause beside the broken road, and the voices of your ancestors rise in the quiet between thoughts.
reason: Align the narrative with ancestral memory and the Elves’ interconnected minds.

original: The Wood Whispers
reason: The trait is no longer woodland-specific; Nature’s Whispers matches the broader living-sign reading.

original: In woodland, gain 1 Boon to a consequential roll interpreting living signs of nearby disturbance. The signs can indicate a general direction, not an unseen creature’s exact square; this does not bypass Hidden.
revised: Gain 1 Boon to a roll interpreting living signs.
reason: Bruce simplified the trait to one Boon on any roll interpreting living signs, with no terrain or disturbance qualifier.
notes: Stable ID unchanged; simple one-line rule.

original: You may rest in a quiet waking reverie instead of sleeping, remaining aware of nearby ordinary sights and sounds. It grants no automatic detection, extra downtime work, shorter treatment interval or Grit recovery. Magical Asleep still works normally.
revised: You may rest in a quiet waking reverie instead of sleeping. You remain aware of nearby ordinary sights and sounds, but this is not automatic detection and does not reveal Hidden or subtle threats. The reverie counts as sleep for rest and recovery, but grants no extra downtime work, shorter treatment interval or Grit recovery.
reason: Bruce approved the clarified rest/awareness wording and removed the unnecessary Magical Asleep sentence.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. No Magical Asleep clause.

original: Gain 1 Boon to rolls affected by Frightened. Resolve the Boon and Banes normally; you are not immune to fear.
revised: Gain 1 Boon to rolls affected by Frightened. Your maximum HP increases by 1. Resolve the Boon and Banes normally; you are not immune to fear.
reason: Bruce approved adding +1 maximum HP to make Bigger on the Inside the Halfling durability trait and close the ancestry HP gap.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. Fear Boon retained.

original: HP +1; base Speed 5.
reason: Halflings are Small; the Foundry token footprint is 0.5 × 0.5.
notes: Downstream: Foundry actor size Small; token width/height 0.5.

original: You fit through openings the DA judges suitable for your actual small size, and gain 1 Boon to hiding behind ordinary furniture that plausibly conceals you. Standing creatures still block their squares; no free movement through enemies.
revised: You gain 1 Boon to hiding. When you are adjacent to a standing creature at least one size larger than you, you can attempt to hide behind it, even in combat and with no other cover, as long as it is between you and the observer. The creature can be an ally or an enemy.
reason: Bruce replaced the squeeze/furniture implementation with an unconditional hiding Boon and a larger-creature cover clause. Positive wording only.
notes: Stable ID unchanged; Size Small required.

original: Quiet as a Burrow
reason: The trait is being replaced with a social/verbal ability; the old name no longer fits.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: You ease your heel onto the floor and lift the latch with the care of someone coming home to a sleeping household.
revised: You let the accusation hang, then answer with the one question nobody wanted asked.
reason: Align the narrative with negotiation, argument and defending actions.

original: Gain 1 Boon to quiet movement outside combat. On a Strong result, one willing companion following your route gains 1 Boon to their next quiet-movement roll this scene. You cannot confer Hidden by walking in open view.
revised: Gain 1 Boon to Guile rolls to negotiate or argue. When you use Guile to defend your own or an ally’s actions, gain 2 Boons instead.
reason: Bruce replaced Quiet as a Burrow with Quick Tongue: 1 Boon to negotiate/argue, 2 Boons to defend own or ally actions.
notes: Stable ID retained; positive wording only.

original: Once per day, before a roll that uses an attribute, gain 1 Boon. Describe a small piece of good fortune. No reroll after seeing the result and no effect on inventory dice.
revised: Once per day, before a roll that uses an attribute, gain 3 Boons. Describe a small piece of good fortune.
reason: Bruce made the once-per-day luck impactful at the system Boon cap of 3.
notes: Stable ID unchanged; legally 3 net Boons at the cap. Negative no-reroll/inventory sentence removed.

original: Second Breakfast
reason: Replace the weak inventory-check trait with a pockets/capacity trait.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: You break the bread, tuck the smallest crumbs into the wrapping and make room beside you for a second breakfast.
revised: Your coat has pockets. Those pockets have pockets. Somewhere in there is a spoon you forgot you packed.
reason: New narrative for the pockets-with-pockets fantasy.

original: When sharing a food bundle with one companion during a safe meal, make one inventory check for the two of you instead of one each. Food is still required; this grants no healing, resistance or extra recovery.
reason: Bruce replaced Second Breakfast with Endless Pockets: +1 Bulk capacity from well-placed pockets.
notes: Stable ID retained. Encumbrance is the penalty; capacity is the correct rules term.

original: Maximum HP +1. Describe the ordinary hardship that taught you to keep going.
revised: Maximum HP +1. You gain 1 Boon to Fortitude rolls to resist death marks. Describe the ordinary hardship that taught you to keep going.
reason: Bruce approved a Human-specific survival rider: +1 HP and 1 Boon to Fortitude rolls to resist death marks.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. Differentiates Human from Dwarf Hard as Bedrock.

original: Road in the Blood
reason: Replace the travel trait with a character-building flexibility trait.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: You settle your pack higher on your shoulders and lengthen your stride toward the next rise.
revised: You watch, try, fail once, and come back with the trick.
reason: Align the narrative with adaptability and learning.

original: Base Speed +1. Long journeys remain ordinary travel; this creates no exhaustion rule.
revised: You gain 1 additional DP at each level, including level 0.
reason: Bruce replaced Road in the Blood with Adaptable: +1 additional DP per level.
notes: Stable ID retained. Downstream Foundry progression must add +1 DP to each level pool, including level 0.

original: You greet a stranger in the words of another home, smiling as they answer in the same tongue.
revised: You greet a stranger in the words of another home, and by the end of the evening you have learned the shape of their craft.
reason: The trait now teaches a foreign trait as well as a language; the narrative reflects that.

original: Know two additional ordinary spoken languages. Choose the communities that taught you; this does not grant a second culture’s discipline or card.
revised: Choose another ancestry. You learn one language native to that ancestry and gain one trait from that ancestry’s trait list as this trait’s benefit. You keep your Human base HP and Speed.
reason: Bruce replaced the language-only benefit with one native language plus one trait borrowed from another ancestry.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. The borrowed trait is the benefit of this trait, not a third ancestry trait.

original: Make Room at the Fire
reason: Replace the weak hospitality trait with a creative tool-building trait.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: You shift a bowl toward the stranger and offer a place beside the fire before asking their name.
revised: You look at the broken cart, the loose rope and the bent nail, and see a solution.
reason: New narrative for human ingenuity and improvisation.

original: Once per scene, when you offer genuine food, shelter or shared work to a nonhostile person, gain 1 Boon to the next Guile roll seeking ordinary hospitality or trust from them before the scene ends. No automatic friendship or compelled response.
revised: Once per scene, you can assemble a temporary tool, implement or weapon from nearby materials. Gain 1 Boon to the next roll you make using it. The tool lasts until the end of the scene.
reason: Bruce replaced the hospitality trait with Ingenuity: once per scene, build a temporary tool/implement/weapon for 1 Boon.
notes: Stable ID retained. Positive wording only.

original: Once per day, declare before an ordinary noncombat roll that you are taking the difficult way on purpose. Gain 1 Boon. You still need a plausible method and any specialist permission; this does not change a card’s attribute.
revised: Once per day, before an ordinary noncombat roll, describe the difficult way you are taking. Gain 3 Boons to that roll.
reason: Bruce approved raising The Impossible Streak to 3 Boons, matching the system cap while keeping it noncombat and difficult-approach only.
notes: Stable ID unchanged; positive wording only.

original: Maximum HP +1. Gain no additional resistance from this trait.
reason: Positive wording pass per D-015; removed the negative resistance clause.

original: Gain 1 Boon to rolls to examine or craft with stone. This covers judging craftsmanship, recognizing stone type and origin, reading patina or recent toolwork, finding secret passages or traps built into stone, and spotting weaknesses in stone or stone structures. Obvious construction clues need no roll; this trait does not reveal an untouched wall’s far side.
revised: Gain 1 Boon to rolls to examine or craft with stone. This covers judging craftsmanship, recognizing stone type and origin, reading patina or recent toolwork, finding secret passages or traps built into stone, and spotting weaknesses in stone or stone structures. You can identify obvious construction clues without a roll.
reason: Positive wording pass per D-015; replaced the negative far-side clause with the positive no-roll benefit.

original: The first creature that deals damage to you in each combat becomes the mark of your grudge. You gain 1 Boon to attack rolls against each creature marked by your grudge. A creature remains marked forever, even if it escapes; a creature can be marked only once, and additional damage does not add more Boons. You can hold any number of grudges. This grants no damage bonus or extra attack.
revised: The first creature that deals damage to you in each combat becomes the mark of your grudge. You gain 1 Boon to attack rolls against each creature marked by your grudge. A creature remains marked forever, even if it escapes. Each creature can be marked once. You can hold any number of grudges.
reason: Positive wording pass per D-015; removed the negative damage/attack clause and stated the marking limit positively.

original: In woodlands and forests, you ignore difficult terrain. This includes difficult terrain caused by natural terrain or obstacles, such as roots, undergrowth, fallen leaves and uneven natural ground. Solid obstacles, occupied squares and magically created or manipulated difficult terrain still apply. Your Speed increases by 1 while you are in woodlands, forests or similar wooded terrain.
revised: In woodlands and forests, you ignore difficult terrain. This includes difficult terrain caused by natural terrain or obstacles, such as roots, undergrowth, fallen leaves and uneven natural ground. Your Speed increases by 1 while you are in woodlands, forests or similar wooded terrain.
reason: Positive wording pass per D-015; removed the negative terrain exclusions.

original: You may rest in a quiet waking reverie instead of sleeping. You remain aware of nearby ordinary sights and sounds, but this is not automatic detection and does not reveal Hidden or subtle threats. The reverie counts as sleep for rest and recovery, but grants no extra downtime work, shorter treatment interval or Grit recovery.
revised: You may rest in a quiet waking reverie instead of sleeping. You remain aware of nearby ordinary sights and sounds. The reverie counts as sleep for rest and recovery.
reason: Positive wording pass per D-015; removed the negative detection and downtime exclusions.

original: Gain 1 Boon to rolls affected by Frightened. Your maximum HP increases by 1. Resolve the Boon and Banes normally; you are not immune to fear.
revised: Gain 1 Boon to rolls affected by Frightened. Your maximum HP increases by 1. Resolve the Boon and Banes normally.
reason: Positive wording pass per D-015; removed the negative fear-immunity clause.

original: Your single-target spell; choose one visible adjacent unoccupied origin square before rolling.
revised: One of your spell attacks; choose one visible, unoccupied square within 6 squares of you before rolling.
reason: Bruce expanded the origin to a visible square within 6 squares and limited it to spell attacks.

original: Your single-target spell may originate from the chosen square. Determine cover and attack path from there, but measure range from you. You must still see the target and cannot cast through an opaque barrier. This changes only the spell’s origin; it adds no roll or action.
revised: Choose one of your spell attacks. It can originate from any visible, unoccupied square within 6 squares of you. Determine cover and attack path from that square, but measure range from you. You must know the target’s location. Roll the spell attack normally.
reason: Bruce approved the 6-square visible-origin version: bend around cover, know the target location, normal spell attack roll.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. Visible origin prevents through-wall casting.

original: You flick a final spark into the ground beside your target’s foot, forcing a stumbling step as the spell lands.
revised: You snap your fingers at the corner of the flagstones, and the trapped gas answers with a sharp, expanding bang.
reason: Align the narrative with the corner spark and expanding gas.

original: Passive
reason: The spark is now an active Maneuver.

original: One creature hit by your Main Action damaging spell.
revised: One corner of your square; each creature in the four squares that share that corner and are in line of effect.
reason: Bruce changed the area to the four squares around a chosen corner, with line of effect.

original: On a Standard or Strong result, after resolving the spell, you may push one of its targets 1 square directly away from you. Use this once on your turn. It adds no direct damage; normal collision rules apply.
revised: Choose a corner of your square and spark a brief flare of gas there. Each creature in the four squares that share that corner, including you, is pushed 2 squares directly away from that corner. A creature in more than one of those squares is pushed once. The spark does not provoke opportunity attacks. Resolve the push as forced movement; normal collision rules apply.
reason: Bruce approved the corner 2x2 area, 2-square forced push, self-push and no-provoke spark.

original: Once on your turn; no benefit from free attacks.
revised: Once per round; uses your Maneuver.
reason: The ability now costs the Maneuver and is limited to once per round.

original: Immediate push after the spell.
reason: The push no longer follows a spell; it resolves immediately.

original: Learn its purpose, whether it is sustained by a creature or an object, and its remaining duration if it has one. The DA also identifies one actual way to end or avoid it, if one exists. Gain 1 Boon to your next roll using that information before the scene ends. This reveals no hidden caster location, grants no dispelling ability, and does not identify an item’s dormant properties or curses.
revised: Learn its origin and purpose, whether a creature or object sustains it, and its duration if it has one. You also become aware of how to end the effect if it is possible. Gain 1 Boon to your next roll using that information before the scene ends.
reason: Bruce expanded the information to origin/purpose/sustainer/duration/end condition and removed the negative exclusion list.

original: One Boon from studying a given effect per scene; reexamining it does not refresh that Boon.
revised: One Boon from a given effect per scene.
reason: Positive wording pass; same limit.

original: One visible ongoing magical effect within 5 squares.
revised: One ongoing magical effect within 5 squares that you are aware of.
reason: Bruce removed the visible-only restriction; the Arcanist can study any effect they are aware of, with no specific sense implied.

original: You catch the approaching spell against a spread palm and twist, sending its pressure back toward its maker.
revised: You catch the approaching spell against an arcane barrier in your spread palm, converting damage into force.
reason: Align the narrative with the barrier-and-force conversion.

original: Self or one willing ally within 3 squares, before its defense against a spell.
revised: Self, before your defense against a spell. The point of impact is one corner of your square.
reason: Bruce made Arcane Deflection self-only and defined the impact as a corner of the caster’s square so the caster is included.

original: Grant 2 Boons to that defense, including a defense against an area spell. After a Strong defense, you may push the visible caster 1 square directly away from you if it is within 5 squares. Make no extra roll; this does not cancel the spell or protect other targets.
revised: Roll your defense normally. You take no damage from the spell. Choose a corner of your square as the point of impact. Each creature in the four squares that share that corner, including you, is pushed a number of squares equal to the spell’s raw damage before your defense or resistance, directly away from that corner. Resolve the push as forced movement; normal collision rules apply.
reason: Bruce approved a self-only damage-to-force conversion: 1 square of push per point of raw damage, affecting the four squares around the impact corner, including the caster.
notes: Stable ID unchanged. 1:1 raw damage to push.

original: Cast and Scatter
reason: The new effect is a vanish-and-return cast, not a scatter.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: Your spell bursts from your hands and you follow its recoil into a quick sidestep, robes brushing the space where you stood.
revised: You let the spell tear a hole in the moment, stepping through the space it leaves behind.
reason: Align the narrative with the vanish-and-return effect.

original: Self, after your Main Action spell resolves.
revised: Self, when you cast a Main Action spell that requires a roll.
reason: The trigger is now a Main Action spell with a roll, simultaneous with the vanish.

original: Move up to 2 squares without provoking. Choose a legal route and free endpoint. This uses no movement allowance and does not change the spell’s result.
revised: Take 1 Bane on the spell’s roll. The spell resolves as you vanish from your original position. Choose a free square you can see within 4 squares of that position; at the start of your next turn, you rematerialize there. You are untargetable while vanished. Your current turn ends, and you have no actions or reactions until you rematerialize. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
reason: Bruce replaced the 2-square move with Siphon Cast: +1 Bane, simultaneous vanish, return at the start of the next turn, untargetable, no further actions/reactions.

original: Immediate movement.
revised: Until the start of your next turn.
reason: The vanish lasts through the rest of the round and enemy turns.

original: Leave a Window
reason: The ability now creates connected windows, not an exclusion in an area spell.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: You spread your fingers around a companion’s silhouette and the gathering storm parts around them.
revised: You draw a glowing seam in the air, then another across the room, and the two join with a soft pulse.
reason: Align the narrative with the portal effect.

original: Passive
reason: The windows are created in response to an ally starting their turn.

original: None — no roll
reason: No-em-dash cleanup and clarifies that the Arcanist does not roll.

original: One creature in your area spell, chosen before rolling.
revised: One willing ally on their turn, before they take any action; choose two visible, unoccupied squares within 6 squares of you.
reason: Bruce replaced the area-spell exclusion with a portal pair for an ally.

original: Exclude the chosen creature from every effect of that spell. Determine the least favorable net Boons/Banes from the remaining targets and roll once as usual. This changes no range or area and grants no immunity to later effects from other sources.
revised: The two squares become connected windows until the end of the ally’s turn. The ally can use the windows once at any point during their turn, either to move through one and out the other, spending 1 square of movement, or to make one attack through one window, measuring range and cover from the other. The ally must be able to see the window they use. The windows vanish at the end of the ally’s turn. This movement does not provoke opportunity attacks.
reason: Bruce approved the connected-window portal: one use, either movement or attack, lasting the ally’s turn.

original: For that spell.
revised: Until the end of the ally’s turn.
reason: The windows persist for the ally’s turn.

original: Repeatable; normal action economy applies.
revised: Once per round; uses your Reaction.
reason: The ability now costs the Reaction and is limited to once per round.

original: You turn both hands as the spell breaks, guiding its last rush of force toward the places you want emptied.
revised: You throw both hands apart, splitting the spell into two screaming arcs.
reason: Align the narrative with the split casting.

original: Passive
reason: The split is a Reaction to the Arcanist casting a single-target spell.

original: None — no roll
reason: No-em-dash cleanup.

original: Up to two creatures affected by your Standard or Strong Main Action spell.
revised: Self, when you cast a single-target spell that requires a roll.
reason: The trigger is now the Arcanist casting a single-target spell with a roll.

original: After the spell resolves, push each chosen creature up to 2 squares directly away from you. Choose the order. This adds no direct damage; use normal forced movement and collisions. The spell need not already cause displacement.
revised: You take 2 Banes on defense rolls until the start of your next turn. Choose two different targets or directions before rolling. Resolve the triggering spell twice, once for each choice, with a separate roll for each casting. Each casting uses the spell’s normal range and effects. Pay any costs for the spell once.
reason: Bruce replaced the push with a double casting at the cost of 2 Banes on defense.

original: Immediate displacement.
revised: The two castings resolve immediately. The defense penalty lasts until the start of your next turn.
reason: The split resolves at once; the defense penalty persists through enemy turns.

original: Once on your turn; no benefit from free attacks.
revised: Once per round; uses your Reaction.
reason: The ability now costs the Reaction and is limited to once per round.

original: Fold the Distance
reason: The ability is now defensive magical armor, not teleportation.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: Magic / Movement
reason: The ability is defensive armor, not movement.

original: You pinch a crease in the air and step through it, drawing a companion across with your outstretched hand.
revised: You fold the air around yourself into overlapping plates of shimmering force.
reason: Align the narrative with the magical armor.

original: Maneuver
reason: Creating the armor now takes a Main Action.

original: None — no roll
reason: No-em-dash cleanup.

original: Self and optionally one adjacent willing ally; visible free destinations within 4 squares of you.
reason: The ability now affects only the Arcanist.

original: Teleport yourself to a chosen destination. You may bring the ally to a separate free square adjacent to your destination, also within range. Both destinations must fit their occupants; no opaque barrier may separate either traveler from its destination. Neither traveler provokes, and the ally spends no action.
revised: For 2 hours, you are wrapped in magical heavy armor. You gain physical resistance 3, fire resistance 3 and cold resistance 3. Use the highest matching resistance for each damage type, to the normal cap of 3. The armor is weightless and needs no armor training.
reason: Bruce replaced the teleport with once-per-day magical heavy armor granting resistance 3 to physical, fire and cold.

original: Immediate teleportation.
reason: The armor lasts 2 hours.

original: Repeatable; normal action economy applies.
reason: The armor is a once-per-day capstone.

original: None — no roll
reason: No-em-dash cleanup.

original: Each recipient gains 1 Boon to defenses against spells until the start of your next turn. During that time, each recipient gains Stability 2 for the first forced movement against them, including being struck in a collision chain. Use the highest applicable Stability, maximum 3. This grant expires after that forced movement even if a higher Stability applied; it never reduces distance a second time. This is a ward, not physical cover.
revised: Each recipient gains 1 Boon to defenses against spells until the start of your next turn. During that time, each recipient gains Stability 2.
reason: Bruce simplified the ward to Stability 2 for the full round, with no special first-use or expiry tracking.

original: Until the start of your next turn; mark each recipient’s Stability grant when used.
revised: Until the start of your next turn.
reason: Remove the special Stability tracking note.

original: Reapplying replaces your previous ward; it does not refresh a recipient’s spent Stability grant before your next turn.
reason: Positive wording; reapplication still replaces the ward.

original: Cut and Turn
reason: The ability is now a reckless charging Maneuver, not a turn after an attack.
notes: Stable ID retained for link compatibility.

original: You follow the stroke through with your feet and slip around the edge of your opponent’s guard.
revised: You lower your shoulder and crash forward, blade swinging wide, leaving your guard open.
reason: Align the narrative with the reckless charge.

original: Passive
reason: The ability is now an active Maneuver.

original: None (no roll)
reason: The Maneuver includes a Basic Melee attack, which rolls Brawn.
notes: Original metadata used an em dash; the new field uses the rules term.

original: Self, after your Main Action melee attack resolves.
revised: Self; move up to 2 squares toward an enemy, then make a Basic Melee attack against a creature within reach.
reason: The Maneuver now includes movement and a Basic Melee attack.

original: Move up to 1 square without provoking. On a Standard or Strong attack, you may move up to 2 squares instead. Use a legal route and free endpoint; this grants no additional attack.
revised: Move up to 2 squares toward an enemy you can see. Then make a Basic Melee attack against a creature within reach. This attack is part of the Maneuver, so your Main Action remains available. On a Weak result, deal 1 extra damage; on a Standard result, deal 2 extra damage; on a Strong result, deal 3 extra damage. Take 1 Bane on defense rolls until the beginning of your next turn. This movement follows normal opportunity attack rules.
reason: Bruce combined movement, a Basic Melee attack and 1/2/3 extra damage into one Maneuver, paid for with 1 Bane on defense and leaving the Main Action open.

original: Immediate movement.
revised: The attack resolves immediately. The defense Bane lasts until the beginning of your next turn.
reason: The defense penalty persists through enemy turns.

original: Once on your turn.
reason: No change to the once-per-turn limit.

original: Skill / Movement
reason: The ability now includes an attack.

original: You catch the incoming blow on your guard and turn your shoulders, stepping smoothly past its line.
revised: You catch the incoming blow on your guard, turn it aside and answer with a sharp cut of your own.
